events.title: Compare AAPL and MSFT closing prices over the last 3 months

tasks.goal: Retrieve daily closing prices for AAPL and MSFT over the last 3 months from market_db, aligned by date for comparison and charting.
Draw a line chart comparing AAPL and MSFT closing prices over the last 3 months using the retrieved data, with a short takeaway.

events.difficulty_reason: single lookup for two named tickers over a date range
events.reason: small model not set, used standard

args.query: SELECT max(trade_date) AS latest_trade_date, min(trade_date) AS earliest_trade_date FROM market.daily_prices
SELECT ticker, count(*) AS rows, min(trade_date) AS first_date, max(trade_date) AS last_date FROM market.daily_prices WHERE ticker IN ('AAPL','MSFT') GROUP BY ticker

WITH d AS (
  SELECT trade_date,
         max(close) FILTER (WHERE ticker = 'AAPL') AS aapl_close,
         max(close) FILTER (WHERE ticker = 'MSFT') AS msft_close
  FROM market.daily_prices
  WHERE ticker IN ('AAPL','MSFT')
    AND trade_date > (SELECT max(trade_date) - INTERVAL '3 months' FROM market.daily_prices)
  GROUP BY trade_date
)
SELECT trade_date, aapl_close, msft_close,
       round((aapl_close - msft_close)::numeric, 2) AS diff_aapl_minus_msft
FROM d
ORDER BY trade_date

WITH base AS (
  SELECT trade_date,
         max(close) FILTER (WHERE ticker = 'AAPL') AS aapl_close,
         max(close) FILTER (WHERE ticker = 'MSFT') AS msft_close
  FROM market.daily_prices
  WHERE ticker IN ('AAPL','MSFT')
    AND trade_date > (SELECT max(trade_date) - INTERVAL '3 months' FROM market.daily_prices)
  GROUP BY trade_date
), firsts AS (
  SELECT (array_agg(trade_date ORDER BY trade_date))[1] AS d0,
         (array_agg(aapl_close ORDER BY trade_date))[1] AS a0,
         (array_agg(msft_close ORDER BY trade_date))[1] AS m0
  FROM base
)
SELECT b.trade_date,
       round(b.aapl_close::numeric, 2) AS aapl_close,
       round(b.msft_close::numeric, 2) AS msft_close,
       round((b.aapl_close / f.a0 - 1) * 100, 2) AS aapl_pct_change,
       round((b.msft_close / f.m0 - 1) * 100, 2) AS msft_pct_change
FROM base b CROSS JOIN firsts f
WHERE b.trade_date IN (f.d0, (SELECT max(trade_date) FROM base))
ORDER BY b.trade_date

WITH base AS (
  SELECT trade_date,
         max(close) FILTER (WHERE ticker = 'AAPL') AS aapl_close,
         max(close) FILTER (WHERE ticker = 'MSFT') AS msft_close
  FROM market.daily_prices
  WHERE ticker IN ('AAPL','MSFT')
    AND trade_date > (SELECT max(trade_date) - INTERVAL '3 months' FROM market.daily_prices)
  GROUP BY trade_date
)
SELECT round(min(aapl_close)::numeric,2) AS aapl_min, round(max(aapl_close)::numeric,2) AS aapl_max,
       round(min(msft_close)::numeric,2) AS msft_min, round(max(msft_close)::numeric,2) AS msft_max,
       round(avg(aapl_close)::numeric,2) AS aapl_avg, round(avg(msft_close)::numeric,2) AS msft_avg,
       count(*) AS trading_days
FROM base

events.text:
We pulled both series straight from `market.daily_prices` (unadjusted `close`, both in USD on NMS, so directly comparable), covering 65 trading days from 2026-08-13 through the latest trade date in the data, 2026-11-12 — no other agent inputs were provided, so there was nothing to cross-check against our own figures.

Headline comparison (as of trade_date 2026-11-12):

| Metric | AAPL | MSFT |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Close on 2026-08-13 | $305.26 | $496.88 |
| Close on 2026-11-12 (latest) | $354.88 | $523.00 |
| 3-month change | +16.25% | +5.26% |
| 3-month low (close) | $305.26 (2026-08-13) | $480.35 (2026-08-17) |
| 3-month high (close) | $355.63 (2026-11-11) | $555.80 (2026-11-04) |
| 3-month average close | $332.66 | $512.89 |
| Gap at 2026-11-12 (AAPL − MSFT) | −$168.12 | — |

Month-end closes:

| Date | AAPL close | MSFT close |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-08-31 | $316.85 | $507.29 |
| 2026-09-30 | $333.02 | $512.90 |
| 2026-10-30 | $344.63 | $521.91 |
| 2026-11-12 | $354.88 | $523.00 |

AAPL rose steadily and made its high on the final day, while MSFT peaked on 2026-11-04 and drifted lower into mid-November, so AAPL outperformed by about 11 percentage points over the window. The chart follows.
